key_agent_trends: Always-on personal agents expand to lower-priced consumer tiers as OpenAI tests Dots with select ChatGPT Plus users.
Enterprise computer-use capabilities mature with admin controls: Anthropic opens Claude computer use beta to Team and Enterprise plans, off by default.
Financial institutions formalize liability for third-party AI agents, shifting risk to customers for autonomous actions in accounts.
Agent infrastructure advances with scheduled web monitoring APIs that push only relevant changes to agents via webhooks.
Offensive AI agents demonstrate real-world impact, with multi-agent systems discovering and exploiting zero-days in minutes.

stories.headline: OpenAI tests always-on Dots agents with select ChatGPT Plus users, expands to Business Standard
stories.what_happened: OpenAI began testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of ChatGPT Plus subscribers outside the EEA, UK, and Switzerland. The company is also rolling Dots out to eligible US Business Standard members. Each Dot runs on its own cloud computer, works in the background toward goals, connects to thousands of apps via plugins, and is powered by models such as GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra. Official help documentation confirms the gradual rollout.
stories.why_it_matters: Extending always-on agents from high-tier plans to the popular $20 Plus tier accelerates mainstream adoption of proactive, persistent agents and intensifies competition with similar offerings from Google and Microsoft.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens Claude computer use beta to Team and Enterprise plans with admin controls
stories.what_happened: On November 20, Anthropic added computer use (beta) to Claude Team and Enterprise plans. The feature lets Claude see a user's screen and operate permitted desktop apps in the new unified Claude experience. It is off by default; only Owners can enable it, with role restrictions on Enterprise, app allow/block lists, and MDM controls. Rollout is gradual to organizations.
stories.why_it_matters: Bringing controlled computer-use agents to business plans enables enterprise adoption of desktop automation while addressing security and governance concerns through admin-only activation and granular restrictions.

stories.headline: Major US banks update terms to make customers liable for third-party AI agent actions in accounts
stories.what_happened: Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, and PNC have revised customer agreements or issued warnings regarding AI agents. Wells Fargo's updated Online Access Agreement, effective around November 24, states that use of any AI Agent is at the customer's own risk and holds users responsible for agent activities until revocation is notified. JPMorgan bans external agents logging in with credentials. Banks are building their own agents while restricting third-party access.
stories.why_it_matters: As AI agents gain the ability to act on financial accounts, banks are clarifying that customers bear the liability for mistakes, unauthorized actions, or prompt-injection risks, shaping the legal and practical boundaries of agentic finance.

stories.headline: Perplexity launches Monitor API to push scheduled web and page changes to AI agents via webhooks
stories.what_happened: Perplexity released the Monitor API, which runs scheduled web searches or page checks and delivers only relevant changes to applications or AI agents through webhooks. It supports Search monitors for topics and Page monitors for up to 10 specific URLs, with a judging model filtering for relevance and freshness. Pricing is $1 per 1,000 successful runs or fetched URLs. Available now via the Perplexity API.
stories.why_it_matters: It enables agents to stay continuously informed about changing information without constant polling, reducing token costs and improving responsiveness for research, monitoring, and proactive workflows.
